newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks edge up in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks edge up in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks firmed from a weak start in early trade on Thursday morning, with the market expected to resume its uptrend despite the decline in the Dow, brokers said.
"With (October) futures expiring soon, there is more volatility, so the uptrend may be uneasy at times," said one broker with an international house.
The Hang Seng Index put on 25 points in the first 40 minutes of trade to 12,516.96. Turnover was relatively robust at HK$1.48 billion.

The market opened down due to overnight weakness in the Dow and London traded stocks, brokers said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 25 points at 6,036, after shedding nearly 70 points at one point and dipping below the critical 6,000 level.
Meanwhile, overnight selling pushed Hong Kong's London Reference Index down to close off 70 points.
Technical analysts were generally upbeat on the market's near-term outlook.
"I expect the correction to hold above 12,430," said Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities. We will see a minor down gap at the opening, then the index should resume the rally today."
Wong said minor resistance lies at 12,540. If the index breaks above this level, the next two targets would be 12,602, the market's previous high, and then 12,730.
The finance and property sectors led the market, with utilities lagging under selling pressure.
The outlook for market leader HSBC is still bullish, said Wong.

"I expect HSBC to test HK$160.00 by early next week," he added. The share was up HK$0.50 to HK$157.50 to match its all time high in early morning trade. Traded volume was also substantial at HK$233.10 million.
The market's smaller quality banks were also up, partly due to fundamentals and partly to interest sparked by the covered warrants issued on five small and medium-sized banks.
Of those, Dah Sing Financial rose HK$0.30 to HK$27.05 and Wing Hang Bank gained HK$0.10 to HK$31.10.
Consolidated Electric Power gained HK$0.20 to HK$18.05, a 1996 high for the stock. Parent Hopewell added HK$0.05 to HK$5.50.
